text.p: Bangladesh's foodgrain output in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending June 30 was expected to reach a record 20.3 million tonnes, Bengali newspaper Ittefaq reported on Thursday.
The newspaper, quoting estimates by government and international agencies, attributed the high production to favourable weather and timely availability of fertiliser.
The newspaper did not give figures for foodgrain output in the previous fiscal year.
It, however, said the country would still need to import an additional two million tonnes of wheat to meet a shortfall.
Government estimates put the country's foodgrain requirement for the current fiscal year at more than 20 million tonnes.
Rice is the main staple for 120 million Bangladeshis, but tastes are slowly swinging to wheat.
Bangladesh's wheat production in 1996/97 was expected to rise 14.5 percent to 1.5 million tonnes.
The newspaper said foodgrain output in the 1997/98 fiscal year (July-June) had been projected at 21.5 million tonnes against a requirement of 20.7 million tonnes.
